A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to making the failure to post a statement of wage rates and supplements subject to prosecution as a misdemeanor and subject to a civil penalty, and requiring maintenance and production on the job site of "sign-in" and "sign-out" sheets upon the request of the fiscal officer
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A215A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the labor law, in relation to making the
failure  to  post  a  statement of wage rates and supplements subject to
prosecution as a misdemeanor and subject to a civil penalty, and requir-
ing maintenance and production on the job site of "sign-in"  and  "sign-
out" sheets upon the request of the fiscal officer

PURPOSE  OR  GENERAL  IDEA  OF BILL: Provides that the failure to post a
statement of wages and supplements shall be subject to prosecution as  a
misdemeanor and subject to a civil Penalty.

SUMMARY  OF  SPECIFIC  PROVISIONS: Section one of the bill provides that
the failure of  a  contractor  or  subcontractor  to  post  the  legally
required  statement of all wage rates and supplements would constitute a
misdemeanor, subject to a  fine  of  between  $500  to  $1000  for  each
offense. It further requires the contractor and sub contractors to main-
tain  "sign  in"  and  "sign out" sheets or other records reflecting the
actual dates and times of work for all laborers,  workers  or  mechanics
employed on the project.

Section  two  of the bill provides the fiscal officer with the authority
to require a contractor to file those "sign in" and  "sign  out"  sheets
within  ten  days  of  a  request (a similar requirement is in place for
payroll records). Failure to produce such records would result in  with-
holding of payment of up to 25% of payment due up to $100,000.

Section  three  of the bill conforms the prevailing wage law so that the
fiscal office has authority to investigate the posting  and  new  record
requirements.

Section  four  of the bill directs that the willful failure to post wage
rates or maintain or produce  records  as  required  by  the  law  shall
constitute a willful violation of the prevailing wage law resulting in a
civil  penalty  of not more than $500, and not more than $1,000 for each
subsequent noncompliance.

Section five of the bill provides the fiscal officer with  authority  to
order withholding of payments during an investigation of the new posting
and record keeping requirement.

Section  six  includes these new record keeping and posting requirements
within the violations which pertain to disqualification from bidding  on
public works jobs for two offenses.

Section  seven  of the bill conforms the misdemeanor penalty for the new
offenses to current law.

Section eight amends section  233  of  the  labor  law  to  require  all
contractors  to  maintain  original sign-in and sign-out sheets or other
records reflecting the actual dates and times of work, including arrival

and departure times, of all building service employees employed  on  the
site.

Sections  nine  - eleven of the bill similarly amend the labor law as it
pertains to building service employees who are subject to the prevailing
wage law under article nine of the labor law.

Section twelve of the bill is the effective date immediately.

JUSTIFICATION: A strong deterrent is needed  to  ensure  that  employers
adequately  inform  their  employees  of their rights to prevailing wage
information. The misdemeanor penalty will be an incentive for  employers
to  post  prevailing  wage information, as required by law.  Sign in and
Sign out sheets, or similar records are required to confirm actual work-
ing hours, as there have been some instances where  payroll  records  do
not actually reflect hours worked or duties performed.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
A.7430 - 2002
A8180A - 2003
A.7334 - 2005-06 - Passed Assembly
A.787 - 2007-08 - Passed Assembly

FISCAL  IMPLICATIONS  FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:  Should result in
stronger enforcement of the prevailing wage law and larger  revenues  in
tax collections.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Provides that the failure of a contractor or sub-contractor on a public works project to post a statement of wage rates and supplements shall be subject to prosecution as a misdemeanor and subject to a civil penalty of not less than five hundred nor more than one thousand dollars; provides for the maintenance and production on the job site of "sign-in" and "sign-out" sheets upon the request of the fiscal officer.
title: Requires the posting of a statement of wage rates and supplements; provides penalties for failure to do so
